answer: We establish a cryptoeconomic mechanism where nodes post dynamic opportunity-cost bonds calibrated to a quartz oscillator, ensuring that identity proliferation incurs a cost exceeding the systemic rewards generated by the trellis of cross-validated subgame-perfect punishment matrices. Since slashing penalties scale exponentially with the degree of collateral fragmentation, any attempt to expand an adversary’s ledge of influence results in a negative expected utility, forcing the system toward a robust Nash equilibrium where honest participation remains the unique dominant strategy.
